validity.recommendation: Narrow FuelSource to 'Texas Eastern Transmission' only. FERC's 2019 certificate order (Docket Nos. CP17-66/67) states Gator Express Phase I ('Southwest Lateral TGP') has new interconnections with BOTH Tennessee Gas Pipeline and Texas Eastern Transmission, while Phase II ('Southwest Lateral TETCO', this row) loops the Phase I TGP segment and 'provide[s] service from the Texas Eastern interconnection to the LNG terminal' -- Phase II has no Tennessee Gas interconnection of its own. EIA's project note for this exact row (Historical Projects sheet, row 1106) independently agrees, describing only 'interconnection with TETCO (Southwest Lateral TETLP)' for Phase 2, with no mention of Tennessee Gas. The current sheet value 'Tennessee Gas Pipeline Company connections , Texas Eastern Transmission' appears to be the whole-project figure (which legitimately applies to Phase 1/P0193, not in this batch) copied onto this Phase 2 row.
validity.researcher_notes: Existence, classification and duplicate status are all clean: the pipeline is real, well documented (FERC Docket Nos. CP17-66-000 / CP17-67-000, EIA Natural Gas Pipeline Projects workbook row 1106, Venture Global's own SEC DRS/A filing, trade press), correctly classified as an interstate natural gas lateral (not a duplicate of the separate P5415 Gator Express Meter Project, which is Texas Eastern's own interconnection/metering facilities at the tie-in point, not Venture Global's lateral -- see cross_row_leads). Length (12.00 mi vs FERC's original 2019 estimate of 11.0 mi new pipe + 0.7 mi built during Phase I = 11.7 mi total, and EIA's exact 12 mi) is within normal as-designed-vs-as-built rounding (~2.5%), not filed as a separate spec concern. Route geometry (../GOIT-GGIT-pipeline-routes/data/individual-routes/gas-pipelines/P3193.geojson: 2 line parts, 9 points, running from about 29.60 deg N/-89.91 deg W south along the west bank of the Mississippi River in Plaquemines Parish to about 29.43-29.46 deg N near the Plaquemines LNG terminal site) is judged an accurate trace of this specific lateral -- right corridor (Plaquemines Parish, from a Texas Eastern interconnection down to the LNG terminal), right project, not the parent LNG plant or a sibling phase. The one real defect found is the FuelSource attribution described above.

Confirms P5415 is a legitimate separate entry, not a duplicate of P3193.
